Fosun Plans Spinoff of Resorts Subsidiary via Hong Kong Listing
By Megan Cheah
Fosun International's resorts subsidiary has submitted a application to list in Hong Kong, joining the ranks of companies seeking to raise capital in the city's bustling stock exchange.

The subsidiary, ClubMed Lifestyle, submitted its listing application on Friday, the Chinese consumer conglomerate said, after it received approval from the stock-exchange operator to proceed with the spinoff.
Details of the initial public offering aren't finalized, but Fosun expects ClubMed to remain a subsidiary after the deal, it said Friday.

Founded in 1950, ClubMed Lifestyle operates 69 premium resorts globally and provides asset-light vacation scenario services. Fosun completed its first investment in ClubMed in 2010, the same year the company opened its first resort in China.
BNP Paribas, HSBC and J.P. Morgan are the overall coordinators for ClubMed's planned offering.

Companies are flocking to Hong Kong to raise funds in what is shaping up to be a banner year for the city's capital market. Funds raised through IPOs for the first seven months of the year totaled 328.2 billion Hong Kong dollars, equivalent to US$41.86 billion, more than double from the same period a year ago, data from Hong Kong Exchanges & Clearing showed.
